explanation: Shrunk scenario is single ball launched upward into ceiling with e=1. After elastic bounce velocity magnitude increases (41.42->41.68->43.3->44.99) instead of being conserved (minus gravity potential change), gaining ~120 J in 3 steps. Cause likely incorrect restitution impulse / positional correction adding kinetic energy on ceiling collision. Changing e from 1 to 0 removes energy gain.
vision_note: A single blue ball starts touching the top edge at step 0 and falls only a short distance in steps 1 and 2, then abruptly appears much lower near mid-height in step 3. This sudden increase in downward travel distance immediately after the ceiling contact shows the elastic bounce accelerating the ball instead of rebounding at conserved speed.
